body: A seed packet leaked into this mailbox. The paper at the bottom is gritty, while the letters above it stayed clean.
title: The parcel under the letters

body: The opened packet is bound with a rubber band. A few dark kernels remain; a second unopened packet is tucked behind it.
title: The returned packet

body: A sack strip and a feed scoop were pushed in here together. The scoop still carries the same dark grains stuck to the strip.
title: The porch delivery

body: These seeds came back with blackened tips. The packet mailed out beside them is still sealed.
title: The garden club exchange

body: A bundle of grain is tied to a map with two pencil circles, one crossed out. The twine is damp with field mud.
title: The wrong doorstep

body: A little jar holds green sediment and a dry seed packet has been folded over its lid. The parcel was too thick for the slot.
title: The sample in a jar

body: A newspaper is wrapped around a withered tomato vine. Its leaves are freckled where field dust collected.
title: The quiet subscription

body: A scrap of duct tape sticks to a sack corner. Two hand drawn arrows show where it was meant to go next.
title: The spare label

body: A sealed sack has been tied to a torn corner from an open sack. Their stitching matches, but only the open one has black dust.
title: The closed loop

body: One packet of corn is damp and swollen; another was packed dry beside it. Someone left both here for collection.
title: The requested replacement
